claims: Artemis II is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission orbiting the Moon.
Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft and Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II reaches a distance deeper into space than any previous human mission.
Artemis II mission type is crewed lunar flyby (no lunar landing).
Artemis II duration is ~10 days.
Artemis II crew is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
Artemis II objective is to validate all deep-space life support and navigation systems for future, long-term human exploration (Artemis IV and beyond).
For Artemis II, the SLS rocket launches from Kennedy Space Center (Launch Complex 39B).
For Artemis II, SLS puts Orion into a high elliptical orbit.
For Artemis II, launch is followed by a translunar injection burn.
Artemis II translunar journey takes roughly four days.
During Artemis II translunar journey, the crew tests spacecraft systems, including manual piloting.
During Artemis II lunar flyby, the crew passes around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II reaches a distance of over 230,000 miles (370,000+ km) from Earth.
For Artemis II, the spacecraft uses the Moon's gravity to aid its return to Earth.
Artemis II demonstrates high-speed re-entry.
Artemis II ends with splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I.
Artemis I occurred in 2022.
Artemis I tested the rocket and capsule's heat shield.
